clusters.name: Security engineering process and an honest, explicit trust model
clusters.description: A published trust model stating which controls are boundaries and which are accident prevention, defensive rules distilled from bugs, invariant tests proven red before fixes, and plain statements of what is not secure.

bestInClass.why: Hermes's SECURITY.md (q5) says the OS is the only boundary and in-process screens are accident prevention, and requires an invariant test proven red for boundary fixes; DeepSeek keeps an enforced defensive-patterns rulebook.

clusters.mechanism: SECURITY.md with boundaries, in-scope/out-of-scope; PR rule: security-boundary fixes ship a failing-then-passing invariant test.

verevon.gap: No baseline record; DOC evidence: a decision ledger, postmortems and honesty contracts. Missing: one published trust-model statement for chat/agent users (which controls are boundaries). A third-party audit/certification of the data-protection design is planned only (v-planned-decisions-148).
verevon.strengths: Postmortem and ledger culture; honesty contracts in the product.

clusters.approach: Keep; write a short public trust model for the agent page (boundaries = Control-signed decisions, bwrap sandbox, Quarry execution; heuristics = injection scan).
clusters.rationale: Verevon equal on process.

clusters.name: Model-facing policy awareness and capability-gated prompts
clusters.description: The model is told the current approval policy and sandbox meaning, policy changes are announced in the conversation, disabled capabilities remove both the tool and its prompt text, and the model is taught not to ask permission via question tools.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek injects the complete policy meaning and announces changes (SRC, e2e-tested); T3 Code removes tool and prompt text together server-side.

clusters.mechanism: System prompt section generated from the effective mode bundle; a policy change appends a sourced system note; tool catalogue and prompt are built from the same server-side capability set.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check whether Do-mode prompts include the effective posture/rung and whether disabled tools are also removed from prompt text.

clusters.benefit: Fewer wasted turns asking for permissions the model cannot get; better honesty with the user.
clusters.approach: model-gateway prompt builder: render posture/rung/network tier from the resolved profile; emit a note on change.
clusters.rationale: Cheap quality improvement.

clusters.name: Interruption guards for running agents (quit/update warnings, hold to quit)
clusters.description: Quitting or updating the app warns which running agents and pending approvals would be interrupted; hold-to-quit prevents accidental exits.

bestInClass.why: DeepSeek names what would be interrupted (DOC); T3 Code hold-to-quit (SRC).

clusters.mechanism: Ask the host what is running before quit; require hold.

verevon.gap: Not needed: Verevon runs execute server-side and survive tab close (runs are durable in session-core).
verevon.strengths: Server-side durable runs make this moot.

clusters.approach: Skip.
clusters.rationale: Desktop-only concern.

clusters.name: Subagent and side-session governance
clusters.description: Delegated subagents only use allowlisted model routes recorded per session; side chats run as read-only forks with deny-all prompting and a breach detector.

bestInClass.why: Claude's read-only side-chat forks (q5 SRC) and DeepSeek's per-session subagent model-route allowlist (DOC).

clusters.mechanism: Subagent inherits a narrowed capability set and an allowlisted model route list; read-only forks deny all prompts and confine reads.

verevon.gap: No baseline record. Check whether depth-1 subagents inherit the parent's posture and capability set (never wider) and whether their model routes are constrained.

clusters.benefit: Prevents privilege widening through delegation as fan-out research grows.
clusters.approach: execution-core: subagent capability set = intersection(parent, subagent profile); record model route policy on the run.
clusters.rationale: Small, defensive.

clusters.name: Declared tool side-effect taxonomy driving policy
clusters.description: Every tool declares a side-effect class (read, read_sensitive, local_mutation, open_world_mutation, external_effect) and MCP-style hints (readOnly, destructive, idempotent, openWorld) that drive approvals, ledgers and auto-review.

bestInClass.why: Manus (SRC) classifies all 22 browser tools into five levels and emits MCP annotations; everything except read/read_sensitive is ledger-worthy.

clusters.mechanism: Static map tool -> side-effect class + hints in the tool contract; policy and approval routing key off the class, not the name.

verevon.gap: The frontend action registry declares risk, approval and reversibility for 168 actions, but execution-core decides risk by substring matching on tool names (delete, write, send, post, exec, ...), which can misclassify (e.g. create_artifact).
verevon.strengths: Typed action registry with risk/reversibility metadata already exists on the frontend side.

clusters.benefit: A declared taxonomy makes approvals predictable, enables auto-review and per-tier connector policies, and removes substring misclassification.
clusters.approach: mp-contracts: SideEffectClass enum on every capability (bound in capability-core's trusted map); execution-core permission uses it instead of substrings; share the same metadata with the frontend registry.
clusters.risks: Mislabelling a tool as read; default unknown tools to external_effect.
clusters.rationale: Foundation for C-t3-11-006, -018 and -038; small effort.
